subject: Geo-fencing & failover for EU/APAC private deployments — ops questions
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@aegisretail.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Park <ben.park@aegisretail.com>, netops@aegisretail.com
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — geo fencing and failover

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Two quick clarifications from our side before we move forward:

1) Data residency constraint: EU customer data must never leave EU jurisdictions for at-rest storage or backups (we can allow ephemeral inference cache out-of-region for <30s but not persist). We also need KMS keys to be held in our EU tenancy.
2) Failover target: For APAC customers we want warm-standby in APAC, for EU customers we want warm-standby in EU — but we also need an approved cross-region failover plan in case a sovereign outage affects the EU control plane.
3) Networking ask: We need clear BGP/peering guidance and an egress firewall profile that prevents any telemetry or logs from de-identifying or exiting to non-approved regions.

Can you confirm Redwood supports separate storage backends per region with control-plane policies that only replicate metadata (no raw customer data) across regions? Also, do you have recommendations for DNS and BGP convergence windows we should plan for?

Attached a short CSV of tenant residency tags we maintain for initial mapping.

Thanks,
Olivia
Product Security — AegisRetail
[Attachment: residency-safe-list.csv (CSV)]

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@aegisretail.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — geo fencing and failover

Olivia —

Thanks for the clear requirements. TL;DR: yes, we can support region-isolated persistent storage + customer-managed KMS for EU, and a warm-standby topology for each region; cross-region control-plane metadata replication is possible with strict filters (no customer payloads). Below are specifics and open questions so engineering can size the design/ops runbook: 

Design notes: 
- Storage: persistent blobs and backups are pinned to the region's object store (e.g., EU-west buckets). Snapshots are encrypted with a regional CMK; cross-region copy is disabled by default.
- KMS: customer-managed keys (BYOK) supported via our KMS integration; we recommend granting Redwood a constrained crypto-ops role scoped to decrypt only per-tenant volumes.
- KV cache & inference state: can be configured to be in-region only or to allow ephemeral cross-region reads with a TTL < 30s (your policy).
- Control plane: metadata replication is limited to routing and health-signal info — we do not replicate model inputs/outputs. This uses an event white-listing filter.
- Networking: we support BGP session peering (primary + secondary) to your edge. We also support an optional transit VPC model for customer peering where BGP announcements are filtered at the onboarding stage.

Operational constraints / SLOs to decide:
- DNS failover approach: low-latency geoproximity with health checks (Route53 latency-based or similar) vs BGP-anycast. Each has tradeoffs on convergence time and DNS TTLs.
- RTO expectations for cross-region failover and warm-standby readiness (we need explicit RPO/RTO numbers for runbook).
- Audit-logging: do you want all audit events stored in-region only? Or central audit aggregation with pseudonymization?

Action items for us: Vivek will draft a network diagram and failure-mode taxonomy; Karthik will validate routing/filtering policies with the runtime team; Laura will prepare a compliance note for KMS scoping. Can you confirm RTO/RPO targets and whether any of the tenants in your CSV require explicit airtight export controls?

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops-network-diagram.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Park <ben.park@aegisretail.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@aegisretail.com>, netops@aegisretail.com
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 02:27:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — geo fencing and failover

Tessa, Vivek —

Quick answers from NetOps:
- RTO: For EU tenants we need a maximum RTO of 5 minutes for control-plane failover and 30 minutes for full data-path recovery to a warm standby within the same legal boundary.
- RPO: Zero tolerated for persistent storage leaving the region. Backups must be retained in-region for 90 days.
- KMS: Keys will remain in our EU tenant; we can establish a restricted decrypt role for Redwood if needed but require hardware-backed keys (HSM).

Network specifics:
- We'll run BGP peering to the Redwood transit VPC. AS-path prepends will be used for preferred active/passive routing; on failover we'll withdraw announcements from the primary and advertise from standby. Expect BGP convergence of ~30–90s depending on path prepends and upstream policies.
- For DNS we prefer health-checked LBs with low TTL (30s) and failover scripts rather than global Anycast — reduces risk of accidental cross-region egress.

Attached an Export of residency tags with tenant criticality.

Ben
Head of Network Engineering — AegisRetail
[Attachment: residency-safe-list.csv (CSV)]

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Park <ben.park@aegisretail.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@aegisretail.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — geo fencing and failover

Ben/Olivia —

Thanks — that level of RTO/RPO is workable but has operational implications. Two items to highlight: 

1) Hot/warm storage topology: To meet 5m control-plane RTO we will keep control-plane state (routing, tokens, health signals) replicated across control-plane nodes in-region and async to standby. However, full data-path (model weights, persistent user blobs) rehydration to warm-standby may take minutes — we'll provide an optimization path using incremental checkpoints to reduce this to your 30m target.

2) BGP + DNS: Ben's suggestion to use health-checked LBs with TTL=30s is straightforward for app-layer failover. We will also offer a BGP withdraw + prepends playbook for network-level failover when upstream peers permit it. Note that prepends may increase convergence unpredictability across different ISPs.

Open questions for Aegis: 
- Do you want automated cross-region snapshot replication disabled by default and subject to explicit per-tenant approval?
- Are we allowed to send anonymized operational telemetry to our central observability (hosted) for product improvement, or must telemetry be stored in-region only?

I'll attach a condensed failure-mode matrix + checklist for tabletop exercises.

— Vivek
VP — Product Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary-failover-playbook.md (MD)]

From: Ben Park <ben.park@aegisretail.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@aegisretail.com>, netops@aegisretail.com
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 07:22:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — geo fencing and failover

Vivek/Tessa —

Answers:
- Cross-region snapshot replication must be disabled by default. Any tenant-level replication requires a signed AMP (account-level policy) and audit trail.
- Telemetry: we permit aggregate, pseudonymized telemetry only. No request/response bodies or trace payloads that could be re-identified may leave EU. Logs containing tenant IDs must be hashed with a salted HMAC before leaving the region.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood provides an updated network diagram showing BGP sessions + prepends and an explicit playbook for withdraw/advertise.
2) Redwood provides sample IAM role policy for the KMS-backed decrypt role.
3) Run a 1-hour tabletop for the EU control-plane failover and capture a runbook with exact CLI commands.

We can host the tabletop on 2028-04-05 09:00 CET if that works.

Ben
Head of Network Engineering — AegisRetail

Ben/Olivia —

Perfect — thanks for the clarity. Confirming actions from Redwood side: 

- Vivek: final network diagram (BGP sessions, prepends, LD/standby annotations) by EOD Thurs (2028-03-23).
- Karthik: draft IAM policy for customer-managed KMS role and HSM constraints by Mon 2028-03-27.
- Laura: compliance note & audit checklist for EU-only audit retention by Mon 2028-03-27.
- Tessa: schedule the 1-hour tabletop for 2028-04-05 09:00 CET; will send calendar invite and a short agenda.

We will also prepare a short extractable playbook with the exact BGP withdraw/advertise sequence and DNS health-check script examples for your ops team.

If there are any tenant-specific quirks in the CSV after we map them to our onboarding, flag them early so we can mark them as "no-cross-replication" in the tenant profile.

Thanks — looking forward to the tabletop.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
